comparison: Both evaluations support the behavioral learning results (C20-C28). OpenEval provides detailed statistical evidence (p<0.001 across multiple measures), while peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings without challenge, noting 'solid analysis' and 'appropriate' experimental design.

Both address distance coding (C29-C31, C53-C55). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to marginal significance (p=0.056-0.058) and unclear interpretation of negative correlations. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming 'brain regions correlated positively or negatively with distance' without raising concerns about marginal significance.

Both evaluate grid-like findings (C32-C35, C44-C47, C61-C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on statistical robustness (p<0.05 FWE-corrected) and sixfold specificity controls. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether effects reflect true social navigation versus sensory/visual confounds, and noting theoretical concerns about grid codes in non-uniform spaces.

Perfect agreement on null EC findings (C36-C37, C67). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this as a 'well-documented null finding' tested with multiple approaches. Peer reviewers accept this result as consistent with theoretical expectations for complex social spaces.

Both address brain-behavior correlations (C49-C51, C77). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on significant correlations (p<0.001-0.032 FWE-corrected). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, not challenging the statistical findings directly but questioning their interpretation given broader doubts about whether neural patterns reflect true social navigation versus sensory processing.

Both evaluate social avoidance correlations (C6-C7, C83). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (p<0.001 FWE-corrected). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with the same interpretive concerns as R8/R5: statistical findings not disputed, but meaning questioned due to uncertainty about whether grid-like patterns reflect social versus sensory processing.

Both evaluate main conclusions (C91-C92). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, citing marginal distance coding significance, absent EC codes, and mixed findings. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether effects reflect genuine social navigation and emphasizing the 2D orthogonal design doesn't generalize to real-world social spaces.

Both address study limitations (C93-C97 in R15; C93-C111 in R6). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting authors appropriately acknowledge methodological constraints. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing these limitations and noting 'After revision, the authors now discuss some of this and the limitations.'

Both evaluate limitations and future directions (C98-C111). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the discussion appropriately speculative with relevant citations. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, with substantial overlap in the specific limitations emphasized (visual confounds, lack of social cognitive processing requirements, non-uniform space concerns).

OpenEval evaluated experimental design and operational definitions (C16-C19, C95-C96) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers did note the experiment was 'designed appropriately' in their general comments.

OpenEval evaluated grid orientation statistical tests (C38-C41) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate use of V-test and Rayleigh's test with mixed results across regions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluated sixfold specificity controls (C42-C43) as SUPPORTED, noting these strengthen interpretation of hexagonal patterns. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this relates to the grid-like findings peer reviewers questioned in R3.

OpenEval evaluated null finding regarding prior literature (C48) as SUPPORTED, noting clear documentation of negative result differing from Constantinescu et al. 2016. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluated tSNR analysis (C69-C71) as SUPPORTED, noting lower EC tSNR but lack of correlation with hexagonal modulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluated comparison to prior literature (C56-C59) as UNCERTAIN due to explicit speculation and marginal precuneus findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C56 overlaps with distance coding claims peer reviewers accepted.

OpenEval evaluated interpretation of grid-like findings in literature context (C60, C63-C66) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate statements about partial replication and reasonable speculation about anatomical connectivity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C60 relates to grid findings peer reviewers questioned.
OpenEval evaluated participant sample and exclusions (C112-C116) as SUPPORTED, noting clear criteria and appropriate sample size. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
